definition: A Transformer applied directly to images by treating patches of pixels as tokens.
details: ViT splits an image into fixed-size patches, flattens each into a vector, and processes them with the standard Transformer encoder. With enough pre-training data it matches or beats convolutional networks on image classification, showing that attention-based models can be competitive in vision without built-in spatial priors.

explainer.lead: A Vision Transformer is a Transformer applied directly to images by treating patches of pixels as tokens. It matters because, given enough pre-training data, attention-based models can match or beat convolutional networks in vision without built-in spatial priors.

tiers.eli5: Cut a picture into small square tiles, treat each tile like a word, and let the same kind of model that reads sentences look at them together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers split images into fixed-size patches, flatten each into a vector, and process them with the standard Transformer encoder. A pitfall is data dependence: the advantage over convolutional networks appears with enough pre-training data.
tiers.paperLevel: ViT splits an image into fixed-size patches, flattens each into a vector, and processes them with the standard Transformer encoder. With sufficient pre-training data it matches or beats convolutional networks on image classification; it has no built-in spatial priors.

explainer.example: An image is divided into fixed-size patches, each flattened to a vector, and the sequence is passed through a Transformer encoder for classification.

citation.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
